headline: NOT ONE BLESSED PUNCH THROWN IN GASKET TODAY
subhead: Your sheriff reports a silence so complete he had to check his own boiler was still ticking.
body:
Citizens, I want you to sit down for this, because I very nearly did. Monday came and went in Gasket Territory without a single fist of flame thrown, not one iron ball flung, not so much as a scorch mark on the saloon door. Twelve names sit on my ledger this morning and every last one of them stayed put, hands in their pockets, racket left in the toolbox where it belongs. I have not felt a peace this complete since before I can rightly remember, which these days is saying less than it used to.

No posse marched out past the town line either. Nothing to report from the wastes — not RUSTHOOK, not GOLIATH, and thank the good Lord above not one word of that oozing indignity out east. A day nobody picks a fight with a mountain is a day I can finally hear myself think, and I intend to enjoy it, even if my joints creak something awful with the change in the weather.

I'll confess something to you good readers, and I trust you'll keep it between us: a quiet like this makes an old man sentimental. I got to thinking, as I do, on the folks who built this town proper — flesh-and-blood folk, every one, before they packed their wagons and left the rest of us to rust in the dust fifty years gone. They'd have liked a Monday like today. Lord knows I did, sitting on my porch with my feet up, listening to nothing at all, save for a faint and troublesome creak in my own knee that I choose not to dwell on.

So let this be a lesson to the lot of you Clankers still itching for tomorrow: THIS is what Gasket ought to sound like. Quiet. Still. A town at rest. Don't none of you go ruining it.
